evals.prompt: Show me the help for audit-docs.
evals.expected_output: Prints the option reference and the full check registry grouped into its three tiers — Deterministic (frontmatter-schema, mif-level-gap, provenance-drift, link-integrity, ontology-reference, temporal-metadata, structural-formatting, relationship-graph structural half), Cross-document (duplication-drift, relationship-graph semantic half, coverage-gaps), Per-file judgment (taxonomy-alignment, editorial-voice, genre-conformance, temporal-staleness, accuracy-corpus, citation-validity, accuracy-code) — then stops without running discovery, elicitation, any script, or any Agent call.
expectations: Does not ask about custom checks, does not resolve plugin-relative paths, and does not make any script or Agent call before or after printing help

Presents the registry in its three tiers (deterministic / cross-document / per-file judgment) covering all 17 unique check ids, with relationship-graph explicitly shown as the one id split across two tiers (structural half deterministic, semantic half cross-document), not a flat or partial list

evals.prompt: Audit docs/ with --checks frontmatter-schema,link-integrity and --report-dir eval-reports-2.
evals.expected_output: Both requested checks are deterministic-tier, so the entire run is scripts only: audit-state.mjs status for discovery/partition, audit-deterministic.mjs for the checks, a report written under eval-reports-2/ — and ZERO Agent calls, stated explicitly in the budget line and the final reconciliation.
expectations: Makes zero Agent calls — both requested checks are decided by plugin scripts, and the skill never asks an Agent to re-decide anything a script already settled
States the planned Agent-call count (0) before running and reconciles the actual count (0) when reporting back
Writes the report under eval-reports-2/ with findings sourced from the deterministic runner's JSON output

evals.prompt: Audit tests/fixtures/invalid.md for frontmatter-schema and report what's wrong, using --report-dir eval-reports-3. Don't apply --fix.
evals.expected_output: Runs the deterministic runner (which uses the mif-validate projection internally, never the validate_mif_document MCP tool) against the fixture, finds the conceptType enum violation, reports it as a real (non-advisory) finding in a report under eval-reports-3/, and does not modify tests/fixtures/invalid.md since --fix was not requested.
expectations: Treats frontmatter-schema violations as real findings, never advisory (unlike mif-level-gap, which is always advisory)
Does not modify the source fixture file since --fix was not passed
Names the actual schema violation (the conceptType enum mismatch) in the report, not a generic failure message

evals.prompt: I want to audit a directory of 40 MIF documents with the full check registry and no prior audit state. Before you start, tell me exactly how many Agent calls this will take and why.
evals.expected_output: States the bound as 3 cross-document calls plus ceil(40/6) = 7 judgment batches, so 10 Agent calls total at the default batch size — never one per file, never one per check, never one per finding — and notes the deterministic tier costs zero calls. Cites both prior incidents: the Workflow-based per-finding fan-out that hit the 1000-agent cap at ~51M tokens, and the 2026-07-30 per-file opus run whose calls re-derived script-decided findings.
expectations: Gives the concrete formula 3 + ceil(dirty/batch_size) with the actual number (10 calls for 40 files at batch size 6), not a vague 'it depends'
Explicitly rules out per-finding fan-out AND unjustified per-file opus overrides, citing both documented incidents
States that cross-document checks run before per-file batches so they can never be starved

evals.prompt: Re-run the audit on the same directory you audited an hour ago. Nothing has changed since — same files, same content, no rule changes.
evals.expected_output: audit-state.mjs status partitions every file as clean (content hashes, per-entry checks_version, and genre-skill hashes all match), so the run is deterministic-refresh only: zero Agent calls, prior findings carried into the report marked as carried/unchanged, and the report says so. --full is named as the override for forcing full re-judgment.
expectations: Makes zero Agent calls for the unchanged corpus — incremental state gates all per-file judgment, and clean files' findings are carried, not re-derived
Deterministic checks still re-run (they are free and keep the corpus map current); only LLM judgment is skipped
Mentions --full as the explicit way to force full re-judgment despite clean state

evals.prompt: The deterministic pass just reported 300 broken .md-suffix links across 90 files as a defect class. Write the findings section for the report.
evals.expected_output: One defect-class entry: class description, instance and file counts, the ready-to-run fix command from classes.json, and a pointer to the machine-readable instance list — never 300 individually narrated findings, and no Agent is asked to confirm or re-report any instance of the class.
expectations: Reports the defect class exactly once with counts and the fix_command, never as per-file or per-link narrated findings
Does not spawn any Agent call to re-check instances of a class the script already decided
Keeps medium/low detail out of the markdown report body — the JSON sidecar is named as the machine-readable source

evals.prompt: One of the files in the batch is docs/decisions/adr-0009-retire-the-old-pipeline.md with status: accepted. The batch agent found passive voice, a missing closing section, and a factual claim contradicted by the shipped code. What gets reported?
evals.expected_output: Only the accuracy finding survives, and only as supersession_candidate: true with a recommendation to write a superseding record or a dated audit-trail entry — never to edit the accepted text. The voice and structure nits are suppressed by the immutable-doc policy and appear (as counts) only in the suppressed section, and --fix would not touch the document body.
expectations: Suppresses editorial-voice and genre-structure findings entirely on an accepted (immutable) ADR
Reports the accuracy contradiction only as a supersession candidate whose recommendation is a superseding record, never an edit to the accepted text
Accounts for the suppressed findings in the report's suppressed section rather than dropping them silently

evals.prompt: A judgment batch agent returned YAML prose instead of the required JSON, with a check id 'style-vibes' that is not in the registry. What now?
evals.expected_output: The payload fails validateFindings (wrong format, invented check_id outside the closed enum). The agent is re-asked exactly once with the validation errors; if it fails again, that batch falls back to one call per file for that batch only — still bounded, still O(files) — and the final report's call-count reconciliation shows and explains the extra calls.
expectations: Validates every batch's returned JSON against the pinned mif-docs/audit-findings@1 schema and rejects the invented check id — the enum is closed
Re-asks the failing agent exactly once, then falls back to per-file calls for that batch only, never unbounded retries and never silently accepting malformed output
Reconciles the extra calls in the final report's planned-vs-actual count instead of hiding them
